differences.what: B's background reads in clear layers (crisp mountain ridges standing above a bright sea of fog), so the depth feels deliberate. In A the upper half is one heavy grey fog bank with smeared, muddy peaks behind it, and the frame looks murky.

B's ridge line of grass tufts shows as clean silhouettes against the bright fog, so the product stands on a defined crest. A's horizon has a dull blue-grey band of water or fog behind the grass that reads flat.
A's foreground grass has warmer, denser backlit rim light on the blade tips and feels more photographic and lush. B's grass is darker and sparser in the near foreground.
B's larger rock frames the speaker on both sides and separates the light cabinet and the chrome horn from the background. In A the rock is smaller and partly lost against the fog.
Tall grass in B covers more of the cabinet's base and feet, so the bottom edge of the product is less legible than in A.

The chrome horn picks up a little more contrast and structure in B because it reflects the darker ridge and the rock. In A the horn and the cabinet faces are slightly flatter and milkier against the uniform fog.
